hints: Look closely at compound X and notice it is a cyclic ester, also called a lactone, with a C-O single bond inside the ring.
Remember that aqueous KOH hydrolyses an ester by breaking the acyl-O bond to give an alcohol group plus a carboxyl group.
Since excess alkali is used, think about what happens to any carboxylic acid formed in basic solution and check carefully which carbon carries the OH.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the functional group in X**

Great start. X is a six-membered cyclic ester (a lactone). The ring contains $-C(=O)-O-$ joined by carbon chains, with a methyl branch on the carbon opposite the functional group.

General ester hydrolysis:
$$RCOOR' + OH^- \rightarrow RCOO^- + R'OH$$

**Open the ring by hydrolysis**

When $OH^-$ attacks the carbonyl carbon, the $C-O$ bond of the ester breaks. The $C=O$ part becomes a carboxyl group and the $O$ part becomes an alcohol group.

So X opens to give one $OH$ group and one carboxyl group on the same chain:
$$\text{lactone} + H_2O \rightarrow HO-CH_2-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-COOH$$

**Account for excess dilute KOH**

Here we have excess aqueous $KOH$, a base. Any carboxylic acid formed is immediately neutralised to its salt.

$$RCOOH + KOH \rightarrow RCOO^-K^+ + H_2O$$
So the organic product must contain $-COO^-$ and not $-COOH$. This rules out the neutral acid structures.

**Check the carbon skeleton carefully**

Trace round the ring from the carbonyl: $-C(=O)-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_2-O-$. After opening, this gives:
$$^-OOC-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_2-OH$$
That is a 3-methyl-5-hydroxypentanoate chain, with the $OH$ on a primary $CH_2$ at the end and the methyl on C3 from the carboxylate end. This matches option A exactly.

options.A: Correct. Ring opening gives $^-OOC-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_2-OH$. The carboxylate reflects neutralisation by excess KOH, and the OH is on the correct end carbon with the methyl in the middle. This is the expected hydroxy-carboxylate salt.
options.B: Incorrect. This shows the correct carbon skeleton but with a neutral $-COOH$ group. In excess dilute KOH, the acid would be deprotonated to $-COO^-$. This option forgets the acid-base reaction.
options.C: Incorrect. This has $-COO^-$ which is right for basic conditions, but the skeleton is wrong. It shows the OH on a $CH_2$ next to the branched carbon ($HO-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-$), which swaps the two sides of the opened ring. Careful tracing of the lactone shows the OH must be two carbons away from the branch.
options.D: Incorrect for two reasons. It has the wrong skeleton like C, and it also shows a neutral $-COOH$ instead of $-COO^-$. It combines the ring-opening position error with forgetting neutralisation in excess alkali.
